name: setgid
description: setgid() sets the effective group ID of the calling process. If the calling process is privileged (has the CAP_SETGID capability), it also sets the real GID and saved set-group-ID. This allows set-group-ID programs to drop privileges temporarily and reengage them securely.

parameters.name: gid
parameters.description: The group ID to set as the effective group ID of the calling process.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: The group ID specified in gid is not valid in this user namespace.
The calling process is not privileged (does not have the CAP_SETGID capability), and gid does not match the real group ID or saved set-group-ID of the calling process.

versions: The original Linux setgid() supported only 16-bit group IDs; Linux 2.4 added setgid32() for 32-bit IDs, with glibc providing a wrapper to handle variations across kernel versions.
